# 8B.8 Research Note: Félix Tshisekedi in 2024

Bottom line: **some real course-correction happened, but mostly late, partial, and uneven.** The strongest positives are technocratic staffing, selective institution-building, and the December military reshuffle. The strongest negatives are persistent security-sector fragmentation, proxy dependence, repression, and repeated evidence that key problems were not meaningfully fixed during the year.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Technocratic PM appointment after coalition uncertainty | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/ | Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa, a planning minister and technocrat, after weeks of post-election uncertainty. This is a real positive sign of adapting method and staffing the executive with a competence signal rather than pure loyalty, though it is only a partial correction and not proof of broad policy repair. | `8B.8`, `4B.2` |
| Finance ministry given to a career technocrat | ACP | 2024-05-30 | https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-fwamba-likunde-un-technocrate-rompu-a-la-tete-du-ministere-des-finances-par-elysee-kakese/ | The finance portfolio went to Doudou Fwamba, described as a career public-finance technocrat with long ministry experience. This supports the view that Tshisekedi sometimes corrected course by replacing purely political staffing with competent implementers. | `8B.8`, `6B.5` |
| IMF-backed fiscal corrections and biometric cleanup | IMF | 2024-07-03 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr | IMF reported corrective measures: biometric cleanup of the civil-service register, social-security reorganization, progress on treasury and expenditure-chain reforms, and improved revenue mobilization. This is strong evidence of administrative correction and resource reallocation, but the same IMF material says progress was slow and the macro gains were fragile. | `8B.8`, `6B.6`, `6B.7` |
| Anti-corruption oversight was publicly reinforced | Présidence RDC | 2024-10-07 | https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes | Tshisekedi publicly backed the Court of Accounts’ control function, and the court credited his support with reviving anti-corruption oversight and public-finance control. This is genuine evidence of course correction through institutions, though it remains executive-centered rather than proof of durable independence. | `8B.8`, `6B.6` |
| Military reshuffle as late corrective action | Reuters | 2024-12-20 | https://theprint.in/world/congolese-president-sacks-military-top-brass-in-major-reshuffle/2411531/ | Tshisekedi replaced the army chief, military intelligence head, and many senior officers. This is the clearest sign he replaced ineffective implementers after severe security failures, but it reads more like damage control than an early or fully successful reset. | `8B.8`, `6B.7`, `6B.9` |
| Task-force coordination and P-DDRCS staffing show active management | Présidence RDC / ACP | 2024-07-05 to 2024-12-20 | https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/securite_a_lest_le_chef_de_letat_a_reuni_la_task_force_du_haut_commandement_militaire/ | Tshisekedi convened high-command task-force meetings, ordered measures to preserve territorial integrity, and later appointed a new national coordination team for P-DDRCS. These are real examples of adapting methods and maintaining control, but they did not resolve the underlying security breakdown. | `8B.8`, `1B.9` |
| Security system remained fragmented despite corrective moves | Reuters | 2024-07-17 | https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/ | Reuters reported mismanagement, weak logistics, demoralized troops, and heavy reliance on Wazalendo proxies the army did not control. Tshisekedi reportedly told them to be brought in line, but the core problem remained unresolved, which is strong counterevidence to effective course correction. | `8B.8`, `1B.9` |
| Political and civic repression suggests weak correction outside the security portfolio | Amnesty International / Human Rights Watch / Reuters | 2024-02-16 to 2024-10-24 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/ | Amnesty and HRW described continued arrests, judicial harassment, media closures, and a militarized state of siege, while Reuters reported a constitutional-reform push that could remove term limits. This is evidence that Tshisekedi did not consistently correct abusive or entrenching behavior, even where the failure was visible. | `8B.8`, `4B.1`, `7B.9` |

## Synthesis
- **Positive side:** Tshisekedi did adapt in several visible ways: he appointed technocrats, backed IMF-style fiscal correction, empowered oversight bodies, coordinated military command, and eventually removed senior military leadership.
- **Negative side:** the strongest failures were not fixed quickly enough. Security remained fragmented, proxies stayed problematic, repression persisted, and the constitutional-term-limit issue moved in the wrong direction.
- **Best calibrated reading:** **some course correction, but incomplete and often reactive rather than consistently effective.**

## Search gap
- I did **not** find a clean independent source showing that the military/security reform line produced a durable 2024 turnaround.
- The strongest positive items are either **executive-hosted**, **programmatic**, or **late-year corrective actions**.
- So the evidence supports **limited adaptation**, not a full “kept advancing the program under effective control” conclusion.
